signals.title: AUD/CHF — G10 Bilateral Theme + Risk-Off Shift
signals.text: AUD/CHF trades under pressure at 0.5483, breaking below its technical moving-average structure as CHF dominates G10 performance. The G10 Currency Strength Scorecard registers an extreme 3.013% leader-to-laggard spread, with CHF outperforming by +1.398% across 6 pairs while AUD drops −1.615% across 4 pairs. RBA at 4.85% vs SNB at 0.00% maintains a +485bp nominal carry advantage for AUD, but acute geopolitical risk in the Strait of Hormuz and an elevated VIX at 26.4 force a rapid risk-off unwind of carry positions. Retail sentiment shows an extreme 84% long positioning in AUD/CHF, exposing retail buyers to capitulation as institutional flows seek capital preservation in CHF. Technical positioning remains weak as AUD/USD trades well below its SMA20/50/200 cluster at 0.6844/0.6943/0.7041. Trade bias: Bearish AUD/CHF, driven by bilateral G10 divergence and carry unwind. Catalyst: US Core PCE and GDP releases at 13:30 UTC. Risk: VIX retraces below 20, halting safe-haven CHF demand and stabilizing high-yield carry pairs.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Carry Support vs Intervention Threshold
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 159.11, holding above its SMA20/50/200 cluster at 158.75/158.12/158.91. A 269bp OIS carry advantage (SOFR 3.92% vs TONA 1.23%) continues to support the dollar, though 160.00 remains the key psychological barrier where official intervention risks intensify. Options markets price elevated downside hedging, with 1M 25d Risk Reversals printing a strong put skew of −1.80 alongside a 1.8% Vol Risk Premium (IV 7.3% vs HV30 5.5%). CFTC positioning shows Leveraged Funds net short JPY at −29,545 contracts, sitting at the 85th percentile of its 52-week range, indicating crowded short positioning vulnerable to verbal or physical MoF smoothing. Cross-asset correlations reflect this tension, as USD/JPY vs VIX registers at z=−2.30σ from its historical norm, confirming JPY safe-haven flows are temporarily subordinated to carry unless intervention occurs. Trade bias: Long USD/JPY, carry-supported below the critical threshold. Catalyst: US Core PCE release at 13:30 UTC. Risk: Direct Ministry of Finance intervention or hawkish BoJ communication forcing a sudden unwind of short JPY positions.

signals.title: NZD/USD — Retail Divergence + Crowded Short Squeeze Setup
signals.text: NZD/USD trades at 0.5459, hovering below its SMA20/50/200 cluster at 0.5557/0.5617/0.5792 in a confirmed downtrend structure. Institutional COT data shows Leveraged Funds net short −23,862 contracts, while Retail sentiment data retail sentiment sits at an extreme 91% long, creating a severe institutional vs retail positioning divergence. Central bank policy rates place Fed at 4.00% vs RBNZ at 2.75%, generating a 125bp carry deficit for NZD that is reinforced by a negative Economic Surprise Index reading of −15.4. However, with OIS markets pricing a hawkish bias for the next RBNZ meeting (mkt: 72% hike priced), any surprise stabilization in domestic data risks triggering an asymmetric squeeze against crowded speculative shorts. The BEER model flags NZD/USD as undervalued at z=−2.04σ (spot 0.5459 vs fair value 0.5556), suggesting structural downside momentum is overextended. Trade bias: Bearish NZD/USD, aligned with macro carry and institutional momentum. Catalyst: RBNZ Board Member comments and upcoming US PCE data at 13:30 UTC. Risk: RBNZ delivers unexpected hawkish guidance, triggering an institutional short squeeze against heavy retail long positions.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Volatility Premium + Options Skew Alignment
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.0946, constrained below its SMA20/50/200 moving average cluster at 1.1094/1.1209/1.1495. Fed at 4.00% vs ECB at 2.65% maintains a +135bp carry advantage for the US dollar, keeping EUR upside structurally capped. Option markets show 1M ATM Implied Volatility at 6.3% against 30-day Realized Volatility of 5.1%, establishing a +1.3% Vol Risk Premium that indicates moderate hedging demand ahead of US inflation data. Directional options skew aligns with downside pressure, as the 25-delta Risk Reversal prints −0.39, favoring EUR put demand over call demand. The BEER fair value model indicates EUR/USD is cheap at z=−2.93σ (spot 1.0946 vs fair value 1.1132), reflecting stretched short-term valuation despite macro headwinds. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD, supported by interest rate differentials and options skew. Catalyst: US PCE Price Index at 13:30 UTC and ECB meeting accounts at 12:30 UTC. Risk: US core inflation prints below consensus, sparking a dollar pullback toward the 20-day moving average.
